subject: Machine Learning
error_analysis:
Final held-out test run, 33 questions (28 answerable, 5 not in the books). Metrics are automatic; answer correctness and groundedness still need human review (evaluation/human_reviews.json).

1. Retrieval (hit rate 53.6%, recall@5 46.4%; target 80%). Validation scored 88.9% on 9 answerable questions, so the test score is the honest figure. Three causes were found:
   a) The page-exact metric undercounts. Several misses retrieved pages that do answer the question, but are not listed in expected_evidence: Q015 retrieved D2L's dedicated minibatch-SGD section (pp. 540-550) instead of pp. 126-127; Q019 retrieved the detailed table of contents (p. 16) instead of p. 4; Q005 retrieved ISLP p. 147, one page before the expected pp. 148-149. With 15 overlapping ML books, many topics are covered on several valid pages.
   b) Cross-book questions (Q030-Q034): a single query embedding pulls all top-5 passages from one book, so the second book is never retrieved (0 of 5 hit).
   c) Long, indirect phrasings (Q021, Q041) drift to loosely related passages.

2. Abstention. All 5 no-answer questions were correctly refused (100%), and citation traceability was 100%: every displayed citation resolved to a stored passage. But 6 of 28 answerable questions (21.4%) were wrongly refused (Q017, Q023, Q024, Q025, Q029, Q042). Four of these had the right page retrieved; the lexical grounding check removed the model's sentences. Numerical answers are hit hardest (Q025, Q029): a computed value such as 0.75 never appears in the passage, so the sentence fails the word-overlap check.

3. Answer quality (from reading the outputs; to be confirmed by human review). Likely incorrect or misleading: Q002 (holdout set described as withheld from both training and testing), Q012 (cites a gradient-style update rule instead of the perceptron rule), Q027 (says no update is needed; the correct answer is an update to w = (3, 2), b = 1), Q032 (claims the Cookbook does not describe splitting, after retrieval missed p. 196), Q034 and Q041 (off-topic answers after retrieval misses). Minor errors: Q009 (writes A as n x m instead of m x n), Q019 (misnames step 2).

4. Speed. Mean 48.6 s and p95 89.3 s per answer on a CPU-only laptop (validation mean: 28.8 s). Cross-book and reasoning questions produce longer answers.

Not done, to respect the held-out rule: the system was not re-tuned after seeing these test results. Candidate improvements, to be checked on the validation split first: hybrid keyword + vector retrieval; one retrieval per book named in cross-book questions; number-aware grounding that accepts values computed from passage numbers; complete expected_evidence lists for topics covered in several books; a stronger project-approved embedding model; and a quantized model runtime for faster demos.
limitations: Retrieval below the 80% target on the test split; page-exact evidence matching undercounts valid pages. Lexical grounding check compares words, not meaning: it can pass a reworded wrong claim and reject a correct paraphrase or a computed number. Small 1.5B answer model on CPU: 30-90 s per answer and occasional wrong reasoning. Evaluation questions and reference answers are drafts written from the book pages and still need subject-expert review. Books 014 and 015 are commercial; their permission is not confirmed. Passages never cross page boundaries; running headers are not removed; equations and tables lose layout.
